questions.prompt: How does fiber-optic cable carry data?
options: As electrical voltage on a copper core
As radio waves inside a metal tube
As pulses of light through thin strands of glass or plastic

questions.prompt: What effect keeps light bouncing inside a fiber's core instead of escaping? (three words)
What's the name of the glass layer that surrounds the core? (one word)
Fiber is resistant to EMI, RFI, and crosstalk.
A cable has to run right beside high-voltage power lines in a factory. Which medium handles the noise best?
Which kind of fiber has a very thin core, uses a laser, and runs for tens of kilometers?
Multimode fiber is the better choice for a 40 km link between cities.
What's a real drawback of fiber?
options: It loses signal quickly over distance
It's more expensive, and the glass is fragile and hard to splice

questions.prompt: What's the key physical difference between Comcast's network and Verizon Fios?
options: There is no difference, both are all fiber
Comcast is all fiber, Fios is all coax
Comcast is hybrid fiber-coax, with broadband coax for the last stretch; Fios runs fiber all the way to the home
Comcast uses satellites, Fios uses radio

questions.prompt: On a hybrid fiber-coax network, your neighborhood's coax segment is shared, so speeds can drop at busy times.
